message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each except one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches either the color, number, or symbol of the top discard. 3. If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise you can be challenged.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20 points, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. The first player to reach the target score (usually 500) wins the game. | | **Optional Variations** | • **Stacking** – allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing.
• **No Challenge** – ignore the “must play only if no other card” rule for Wild Draw Four.
• **House Rules** – e.g., “Draw Two on a Reverse” or “Wild Draw Four can be played on any card.” | **Quick Tips** - Keep an eye on the colors you’re running out of; try to play them early. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Remember to shout “UNO!”—it’s a simple but crucial rule. Enjoy your game!
